Subject: CardioX POC: security intake & isolation diagram request (post-demo)

Hi Daniel / Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time for the demo today — really appreciated the detail on your latency and data residency needs. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture immediate next steps so we keep momentum on the POC and make sure we have the compliance evidence you need.

Quick recap from Redwood:
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in Oct 2027; we can share the full report under NDA and a controls mapping specific to CardioX requests.
- Data residency & GDPR/HIPAA: hosted options are regionally isolated; for PHI workloads we recommend Private (VPC) or on‑prem with our optional encryption/HSM integrations.
- Network isolation / air‑gap: we support a hardened VPC topology and an air‑gapped on‑prem package for regulated workflows — will call out tradeoffs below.

What we need from CardioX to scope the POC and compliance path:
1) A rough network diagram showing where Redwood inference would sit relative to your CICD, data stores, and any egress-restricted zones (simple PNG/PDF is fine).
2) Completed vendor security questionnaire (we noted you have a template) — attach your latest if helpful.
3) Intended workload (training vs inference only), expected QPS, and peak sequence length so we can size a Private instance for the demo.

Attachments: redwood_compliance_overview.pdf (SOC2 summary, controls index, evidence types)

Short answers on air‑gap vs VPC:
- VPC (recommended for most customers): fastest to provision, supports KMS integrations, predictable latency.
- Air‑gapped on‑prem: higher isolation but longer lead time and heavier ops (hardware procurement + on‑site install).

Proposed next steps / owners:
- CardioX: provide network diagram + vendor questionnaire (Daniel/Emily) — due Jan 11
- Redwood: provide controls mapping and a VPC topology template (Sean) — by Jan 12
- Schedule a technical deep‑dive to walk the diagram and our proposed topology (Olga) — propose Jan 13 or 14

Happy to jump on a quick call if either of you prefer a working session to fill the questionnaire.

Thanks,
Olga Petrova
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Olga — great demo and thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side so Sean can scope: 

- We'll be sending you a redacted network sketch by EOD Jan 11. It will show an internal analytics cluster (PHI), our ingestion pipeline, and a DMZ where calls to inference would originate.
- We attached our vendor security questionnaire (CardioX_VendorQ_v1.xlsx) — we've filled the basics, left a few control-specific items blank that need Redwood input (SOC2 control owners, encryption-at-rest details).

One ask re: air‑gapped option — does Redwood provide an appliance image / installable package, or is the on‑prem route fully managed by the customer's infra team? If it's an appliance, what are the minimum hardware and network requirements?

Also copying procurement (<procurement@cardiox.com>) to start the commercial thread; they may want a short statement of work and draft SOW/PO flow.

Daniel —

Thanks for the details and the questionnaire. Quick answers inline and next items for scoping: 

- SOC 2 & controls: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report (Oct 2027) covers system availability, confidentiality, and change management. We can provide the full report under NDA and a controls mapping that points to the rows in your questionnaire where we meet the controls. I'll attach a VPC topology template that maps to each control category.

- Encryption: data at rest is encrypted by default (AES-256); we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Private deployments. TLS 1.2+ in transit; mutual TLS is available for VPC endpoints.

- Air‑gapped/on‑prem: we provide an installable package + deployment guide for air‑gapped installs. It's not a single hardware appliance — instead we deliver validated AMIs/containers and orchestration scripts that your infra team runs in the isolated environment. Minimum recommended hardware for the POC (inference-only):
  - 2 x A100 (or equivalent) GPUs
  - 64 vCPUs
  - 512 GB RAM
  - 10 Gbps internal network fabric

If you want a more turn-key physical appliance, Redwood partners with select integrators for on‑site installs — we can introduce you if needed.

- Sizing: with 30 sustained QPS and 80 QPS spikes at 512 tokens, our initial suggestion is a 2-GPU Private node with autoscale burst to 4 GPUs for peak windows. Marcus, can you produce a quick cost/throughput estimate and a VPC sketch that matches Daniel's future diagram?

Action items: 
- CardioX: upload network sketch + any additional questionnaire fields (Daniel) — target Jan 11
- Redwood (Sean): upload controls mapping + VPC topology template (attached) — target Jan 12
- Redwood (Marcus): POC sizing and cost estimate — target Jan 12

Thanks,
